title: `cat =ls<TAB>`: the `=word` rewrite happens in ARGUMENT position too — zsh lists ls* commands, zshrs rewrites the word to /bin/ls

observed.raw_stream: after `c\bcat =ls` zsh writes the two-column ls* listing, zshrs writes `\b\b\b/bin/ls`
observed.cursor: zsh row 0 col 12, zshrs row 0 col 16
observed.notes: Same defect as `equals_word_line_rewrite`, one word to the right: there the `=ls` is the command word, here it is an argument to `cat`. Pinned as its own fixture rather than as a variant because the fingerprint is DIFFERENT — 3819a12e50 here against f55ac1e11f in command position — and comptab_parity's fingerprint takes the surrounding context in, so a variant carrying the other id would misreport a shape drift as a match. No zstyle on either side: this is `zsh -f` defaults. If the two are ever fixed together they will go NOW-PASSES together, which is the signal that they were one root cause.

origin: reported by a peer agent in round 4 as `cat =ls` diverging at zsh -f defaults; re-run first-hand here before pinning
